v.rationale:
All three suites pass. The three implementations are almost the same: a FormRequest, Hash::check followed by a 401 with the exact message, createToken returning 201, currentAccessToken()->delete() returning 204, /me using only(id,name,email), and a named RateLimiter keyed on lower-cased email plus IP. I ran the same probes against all three and they behaved identically:
- An array `email` gives a 500 in every implementation, because the limiter casts it to a string before validation runs.
- A non-JSON form post still gets JSON 201/401 responses.
- An email padded with whitespace shares the throttle bucket with the plain email (TrimStrings already trims it).
- The 429 response has a JSON message.
- Successful logins also count toward the limit.

So the ranking comes down to idiom and test quality.

impl-3 ranks first: it uses validated() throughout, splits the controllers cleanly, has the most rigorous tests (expiry tested after a real 429, the other token still works after logout) and puts RefreshDatabase in Pest.php.

impl-1 ranks second: the code is nearly the same as impl-3, but the limiter is a long one-liner with a redundant trim(), and it adds a pointless password-hash test and redundant factory overrides.

impl-2 ranks third: it is the leanest, and its email rule is a plus, but it passes Stringable objects into Hash::check and createToken instead of validated strings, it has no test that the throttle window expires, and it declares RefreshDatabase in each file.
